name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkish lira near record low around 50 per dollar under managed depreciation; no major EM default or capital controls
state: The Turkish lira breached 50 per dollar for the first time on 3 Nov as annual inflation rose to 29.8% in October, and has stayed near that level under managed depreciation, a move of about 2% over a month (Shafaq News). Turkey's central bank governor is due to present new inflation forecasts on 12 Nov. No major emerging economy had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF support as of 11 Nov.
for_you: Travellers to and businesses trading with Turkey face a weaker lira and high local inflation. Wider emerging-market strain tends to show first in currencies and bond yields.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency fall > 10% in a month, emergency IMF request, default or capital controls: Normal

sources.title: Shafaq News — Turkish lira breaches 50 per dollar to record low

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
